sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: This lesson is about what you can do: things you are able to do now, things you could do as a child, polite ways to ask, and what you will be able to do. Almost always the action after the key word stays as in the dictionary, with no to.

examples.en: I can remove this stain.
examples.translation: I am able to do it now

examples.en: At ten, I could read fluently.
May I have a sample?
We will be able to achieve this goal.
examples.translation: we can do it in the future

blocks.text: can + the action as in the dictionary: I can remove this stain. can is the same for everyone — he can, she can, no -s. Not able: cannot — We cannot talk in private. Never put to after can.

examples.en: I can remove this stain.
examples.translation: I know how to clean it

examples.en: She can replace the battery.
examples.translation: she is able to change it

examples.en: We can arrange a meeting.
Noise can affect your sleep.
examples.translation: it is possible that it does

examples.en: We cannot talk in private.

fixes.wrong: I can to describe the place.

drill.why: After can: the action as in the dictionary, no -s, no to.

sections.title: could — I was able to, in the past

blocks.text: To say what you were able to do in general in the past, use could: At ten, I could read fluently. could is also the same for everyone and also has no to after it.

examples.en: At ten, I could read fluently.
examples.translation: I read well as a child

examples.en: At six, I could write the alphabet.
At twelve, we could travel independently.
At twenty, I could learn a new skill.

fixes.wrong: At ten, I can read fluently.
fixes.right: At ten, I could read fluently.

fixes.wrong: At ten, I could to read fluently.
fixes.right: At ten, I could read fluently.

drill.question: You remember your childhood: at ten you already read well. What do you say?
drill.optionA: At ten, I can read fluently.
drill.optionB: At ten, I could read fluently.
drill.explain: An ability in the past: could.

blocks.text: To ask for permission politely, say May I + the action? May I have a sample? May comes first, before I, and the action after I has no to.

examples.en: May I have a sample?
May I make a comment?
May I change the channel?
May I disturb you for a moment?
May I check the exact price?

fixes.wrong: May I to have a sample?

blocks.text: Could I…? is another polite way to ask: Could I pay in advance? Here could is not about the past; it is a request. Same order: Could first, then I and the action with no to.

examples.en: Could I discuss my diet?
Could I bring my sibling?
Could I pay in advance?
Could I start right away?
Could I have it in writing?

fixes.wrong: Could I to discuss my diet?

drill.prompt: Ask politely if you can pay all the money at once.

sections.title: be able to — now and in the future

blocks.text: am / is able to + action means the same as can, with am / is and to: I am able to cope with the stress. For the future use will be able to: We will be able to achieve this goal. Never say will can.

formula.text: now: am / is able to + action
future: will be able to + action

examples.en: I am able to cope with the stress.
She is able to recover at home.
I am able to concentrate here.
We will be able to achieve this goal.
We will be able to pay this debt.

fixes.wrong: We will can achieve this goal.
fixes.right: We will be able to achieve this goal.

fixes.wrong: I able to cope with the stress.
fixes.right: I am able to cope with the stress.

fixes.wrong: I am able cope with the stress.
fixes.right: I am able to cope with the stress.

drill.why: In the future: will be able to. will can does not exist.

fixes.wrong: I can to describe the place.
I am able cope with the stress.
fixes.right: I am able to cope with the stress.

fixes.wrong: We will can achieve this goal.
fixes.right: We will be able to achieve this goal.

blocks.text: After can, could, May I and Could I comes the action as in the dictionary, with no to. In able to you do need to, with am / is or will be before it.
Able now — can. Able in the past — could. Asking politely — May I…? or Could I…?. Able in the future — will be able to. No to after can and could; to after able.

examples.en: I can keep up with you.
examples.translation: I can go as fast as you

examples.en: May I offer an apology?
She is able to participate in the class.
